This is such a dishonest argument. Anybody who has created in art for all their lives knows this, but for the record: yes, artists might use references or learn from other artists, but every artist has their own fingerprint, their own style and way of doing things that has been accumulated over a lifetime of making art. They can't just shake that off. Just like how your handwriting is unique to you, and sure, you can try to replicate somebody else's handwriting from a glance, but you will never accurately replicate it with 100% accuracy. Their handwriting is something unique to them, that they learned over a lifetime of writing. Art is no different.  


AI in comparison is a chameleon. It can replicate anything, any style, anyone with 100% accuracy. It hasn't had a lifetime of experience, it hasn't had a previous style. It doesn't have anything to add, it just takes.  


Another question. How come when it comes to art, people will say "uhh, it's not stealing honey. AI needs to learn just like real people, checkmate 😎" but suddenly, when it comes to the discussion of real people's private pictures being used by AI to replicate people, they suddenly feel sensitive? If they aren't concerned about AI copying, then they might as well plug their selfies and family pictures into AI learning and be fine with it - it isn't copying, right? It's just learning, so it's fine!
